name: Build advice
blurb: Star ratings and what each background and feat really does for a character, plus quick background picks for every class.
contents: Ratings and player impact for 96 feats
Quick picks for 13 classes in character creation
about: An editorial shortlist from your backgrounds and feats workbook (compiled October 2026). Ratings are opinions; play what you enjoy.

Alert: Top-tier. Acting first decides many fights, and the swap lets you put your best controller or healer at the top of the order.
Crafter: Economy and utility only. The discount matters most when buying expensive armour at low levels.
Healer: Turns the party's Hit Dice into in-combat healing; useful in parties without a dedicated healer.
Lucky: Strong and universal. It scales with level and works on attacks, saves and checks.
Magic Initiate: Best-in-class flexibility: Guidance, Shield, Healing Word, Goodberry, Find Familiar and more at level 1.
Musician: A party-wide reroll engine that synergises with Tireless Reveler, Zhentarim Ruffian (Family First) and other Inspiration feats.
Savage Attacker: A modest damage bump (about +1 to +3 average), best with big weapon dice; doesn't affect Sneak Attack or Smite dice.
Skilled: Pure breadth. Good for skill-monkeys and party faces, but adds no combat power.
Tavern Brawler: Great for grapplers and monks (a free push each turn sets up hazards and Prone combos).
Tough: Reliable durability (+40 HP by level 20) for front-liners and Concentration casters.
Cult of the Dragon Initiate: Flavourful, but the fear costs your action and keys off Wisdom. Better on Wisdom builds that already frighten (e.g., with the Fear spell).
Emerald Enclave Fledgling: Niche. Ritual Speak with Animals is nice utility, but Help-based swapping rarely justifies the action.
Harper Agent: Weak for most builds, since Help costs an action. Better for Mastermind rogues or anyone with Bonus-action Help.
Lords' Alliance Agent: Solid for bodyguard-style melee and high-crit builds (Champion, dual wielders, monks).
Purple Dragon Rook: A good opening-turn party buff; less frequent than Musician but stacks with it.
Spellfire Spark: Excellent. A second damage cantrip each turn on several turns per day, plus passive damage reduction.
Tyro of the Gauntlet: Very situational; Readying is usually a poor use of your turn.
Zhentarim Ruffian: Strong with Sentinel, Polearm Master and big-dice reaction attacks; the party-wide Initiative Advantage is excellent.
Dragonscarred: Fixes the Initiate's action-cost problem and adds a resistance.
Harper Teamwork: A Help-to-debuff combo for a caster ally's next save-or-suck spell.
Lordly Resolve: A strong once-per-day anti-control rally for the party.
Order's Resilience: Minor defensive upgrade for formation fighters.
Purple Dragon Commandant: Good martial support feat; open to any martial via weapon proficiency.
Spellfire Adept: Big burst for radiant casters (clerics, light/celestial builds, Spellfire Spark users).
Zhentarim Tactics: Turns every melee hit you take into a reaction attack (rerolled damage via Ruffian).
Tireless Reveler: Excellent in a party with Musician or Purple Dragon Rook; useless without another Inspiration source.
Vampire Hunter: Strong in undead and vampire campaigns; otherwise situational.
Vampire's Plaything: A free healing potion every day plus Cunning-Action-style mobility; the master is a built-in plot hook.
Child of the Sun: Reliable party-wide Advantage at level 1; the aura is niche.
Shadowmoor Hexer: Hex at level 1 for any class. Best on multi-attack martials with free Concentration.
Aberrant Dragonmark: The only dragonmark open to any lineage, with a Short-Rest spell. Good on Con-heavy martials and sorcerers.
Mark of Detection: The investigator's toolkit, with See Invisibility as the combat-relevant piece.
Mark of Finding: Free Hunter's Mark for any martial, plus strong Perception.
Mark of Handling: Beast-control utility. Find Familiar on the list is a hidden gem for non-wizards.
Mark of Healing: Turns any caster into a backup healer; the spell list is excellent for non-healing classes.
Mark of Hospitality: Mostly social and camp utility, but Aid and Tiny Hut on the list are strong.
Mark of Making: A free +1 weapon each day at level 1, and Spiritual Weapon for arcane casters.
Mark of Passage: Misty Step at level 1 plus speed and grapple-escape bonuses; top-tier mobility.
Mark of Scribing: Communication utility; Command and Silence on the list add some combat use.
Mark of Sentinel: The premier bodyguard feat: free Shield plus taking hits for allies. Counterspell for divine casters.
Mark of Shadow: Invisibility at level 1 is exceptional for scouts and infiltrators.
Mark of Storm: Decent blaster/control list; the Greater Mark's flight is the payoff.
Mark of Warding: Free daily Mage Armor (great for monks-turned-casters, sorcerers, unarmoured builds) and a strong defensive list.
Greater Aberrant Mark: Strong sustain and damage for Con-heavy builds.
Greater Mark of Hospitality: Exhaustion removal is rare and valuable.
Greater Mark of Making: A free upcast Magic Weapon daily.
Greater Mark of Sentinel: Adds a counterattack to every bodyguard swap.
Greater Mark of Shadow: Upcast Invisibility (an extra target) once per day.
Greater Mark of Warding: Strong repeatable defence for the party.
Potent Dragonmark: Turns the Spells of the Mark list into real, recharging magic.
Fey Pact: Solid face and utility pact; the greater feats are the draw.
Infernal Pact: Devil's Sight-style vision at level 1 enables Darkness combos for any class.
Shadow Pact: Released Oct 2026; modest alone, sets up the Shadow greater feats.
Fey Tormentor: Strong party-wide AC debuff once a day.
Infernal Bulwark: Unarmoured AC for casters, considered one of the strongest Drops feats.
Infernal Dragoon: Area fear plus an all-day magic weapon for martials.
Shadow Weaver: Controllable Darkness; best paired with Devil's Sight / Infernal Pact allies.
Sharp Eye: Narrow; outclassed by Skilled or Lucky unless your game is investigation-heavy.
Survivor: A strong Initiative floor plus anti-fear protection; ideal for horror campaigns.
Aberrant Anatomy: Blindsight answers invisibility and darkness, but the Stun drawback is harsh.
Echoing Soul: Excellent skill package; the drawback can cost a turn.
Gathered Whispers: A Shield-like Reaction several times a day; great on armoured characters.
Living Shadow: Reach is great for melee rogues, monks and blade warlocks; the drawback can hit allies.
Mist Walker: Good escape tool, but the Short Rest penalty hurts warlocks, monks and fighters.
Second Skin: Concentration-free Alter Self (aquatic, natural weapons, disguise) is strong utility.
Symbiotic Being: Excellent save insurance for big-Hit-Die martials; the drawback is a big roleplay risk.
Touch of Death: The drawback outweighs a single cantrip; flavour pick only.
Watchers: Weak benefits and a severe drawback.
Arcane Artist: Only pays off for regular Illusion casters.
Arcane Eloquence: The best social origin feat: an unlimited Guidance-style bonus on the three key social skills.
Arcane Infiltrator: Big defensive boost for casters and warlocks; adds little for rogues.
Arcane Omens: Excellent support: Guidance plus repeatable save rescue for the whole party.
Arcane Overload: Fire Bolt is the real benefit; Power Surge is a small once-a-day bump.
Arcane Safeguard: Bonus-action Resistance is good but clashes with Concentration spells.
Arcane Undertaker: Toll the Dead or Chill Touch for anyone; the rest is minor.
Familiar Friend: Find Familiar is one of the best utility spells (Help action, scouting), and this version is sturdier.
Portal Jumper: Action-free teleport escapes grapples and lines of attackers. Great for skirmishers.
Transmuted Anatomy: Strong Concentration insurance and speed for any build.
Elemental Familiar: Gives the familiar a real attack.
Magic Connoisseur: Extends any Magic Initiate background (Acolyte, Guide, Sage, Genie Touched, Moonwell Pilgrim).
Upper Planes Pact: Radiant resistance is rare and matters more at higher levels; the rest is light utility.
Elysium Diplomat: Reviewers call Quick Retreat useful for ranged builds; Divine Calm depends on your DM using the attitude rules.
Ysgardian Warrior: RPGBOT's verdict is 'do not take it'; the payoff is small and situational.
